title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
claim: Capability gains over time and accuracy yield only modest reliability improvements, and all vendors cluster on the same plateau.
layout: 2x2 scatter grid, shared axes, trend lines, r/slope boxes, top legend
description: A 2x2 grid of scatter plots under a single legend bar that shows three providers (OpenAI as green circles, Google as blue squares, Anthropic as tan triangles) plus a black trend line. Rows are two benchmarks: reliability on GAIA (top) and reliability on tau-bench (bottom). The left column plots reliability against model release date, from 2024-05 to 2026-05. The right column plots reliability against accuracy, from 0 to 1. Each panel has a thick black regression line. A rounded box in the lower right gives r and slope. The top-left slope is a shallow 0.03/yr, and the values rise to r=0.92 and slope=0.33 in the bottom right. Points from the different vendors overlap and cluster in the 0.7–0.9 reliability band, so the trend lines look nearly flat. The eye goes first to the colored markers and the flat trend lines.
caption: Reliability gains lag behind accuracy improvements. Overall reliability shows minimal improvement over time, despite 24 months of model releases. Moreover, improving accuracy alone does not guarantee reliability gains on complex real-world tasks. All frontier model providers cluster similarly, indicating reliability is an industry-wide plateau rather than a vendor-specific limitation.
abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed to execute important tasks. While rising accuracy scores on standard benchmarks suggest rapid progress, many agents still continue to fail in practice. This discrepancy highlights a fundamental limitation of current evaluations: compressing agent behavior into a single success metric obscures critical operational flaws. Notably, it ignores whether agents behave consistently across runs, withstand perturbations, fail predictably, or have bounded error severity. Grounded in safety-critical engineering, we provide a holistic performance profile by proposing twelve concrete metrics that decompose agent reliability along four key dimensions: consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety. Evaluating 15 models across two complementary benchmarks, we find that recent capability gains have only yielded small improvements in reliability. By exposing these persistent limitations, our metrics complement traditional evaluations while offering tools for reasoning about how agents perform, degrade, and fail.
